messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw what I think is an "arrhythmia" pattern in model-serving latency across prod-gpu-pools over the last 48h. Three distinct spikes (short, high amplitude) instead of a sustained drift. Need to decide SLO/SLA tuning + remediation owners.

maria: Quick summary: p95 latency spiked ~3x for ~30-90s windows at 02:10, 09:05, and 15:40 UTC. Error budget burn was ~12% in 48h for the affected routes. No correlated deploys. Suspect workload bursts + cache-warm behavior.

aj: which metric are you looking at — p95 or p99? can you paste the dashboard link?

maria: p95 primarily, but p99 shows smaller sample noise. dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/serving/latency?panel=pgp

maria: current SLO snippet (from infra config):
```
service: model-serve
slo_window: 30d
slo_targets:
  - metric: latency.p95_ms
    target: 150
    allowed_burn: 0.005
```

devon: ok. two thoughts: 1) short spikes like this look like transient queueing — we should add a short-window alert (3m p95 > 300ms) separate from the monthly SLO. 2) consider changing operational SLO tiers: keep monthly SLO for customer contracts but add a 24h operational SLO for early detection.

kevin: I can take dashboard + alert work. Plan: add a 3m/15m p95 panel, add PagerDuty rule for 3m breach. ETA: EOD tomorrow for dashboard + runbook stub.

aj: agree on adding a 24h rolling SLO. Proposal: 24h window target 110% of monthly target to avoid flip-flop. e.g., monthly p95 target 150ms, 24h target 165ms. That keeps contract stability but surfaces ops regressions.

maria: noted. Also propose to tighten the error-budget policy: if burn rate > 4x over 6h, trigger a remediation sprint (automated slack message + pause non-critical rollouts).

devon: long-term: investigate cache warm-up and continuous batching settings. I saw spikes coincide with GC-like events on stateful nodes + KV cache misses. Action: add telemetry to KV cache miss rate and batch size distribution.

kevin: creating tasks in the postmortem tracker now.
kevin: Tasks (short):
- dashboard + 3m alert (owner: kevin) — due: +1d
- 24h SLO proposal + stakeholder signoff (owner: aj) — due: +4d
- Error-budget policy update + rollout block automation (owner: maria) — due: +7d
- Telemetry for KV misses + batching (owner: devon) — due: +14d

oncall-bot: incident 2026-04-12T15:41:07Z severity: S3 closed — tags: latency-spike, kv-cache

aj: I'll draft the 24h SLO doc and ping compliance + sales for SLA implications. if customers are relying on p95=150ms, we should include a migration note.

maria: can we also add a dashboard diff panel that shows spike frequency per week so we can detect trend vs noise? small ux ask but useful.

kevin: yes. adding weekly frequency panel and a single-number trend rate.

devon: one more ops note: add a short blameless checklist for runbook steps — restart route? scale pool? toggle batching? so on-call has a concise decision tree.

aj: agree. I'll own the runbook checklist item.

maria: owners + deadlines logged. can we have a quick sync tomorrow 10:30 UTC (15 min) to confirm dashboards and the 24h SLO draft?

kevin: +1 — on my calendar.

devon: +1

aj: +1

maria: thanks all. We'll iterate the SLA language after stakeholder feedback. marking this thread as action-tracker source. :white_check_mark:
